content_html:
I have been a director of engineering for a bit over three years now, and I still hear and read what I call the "old rules" repeated over and over: a director should not spend time coding, good work takes time, protect the team from the business, get consensus before you commit, etc.

For a while I thought the people repeating these lines were behind. Then we introduced LLMs in my org and the cost of producing code dropped, and I started checking each rule against the assumption underneath it. The surprising realization was that about half of the old rules were resting on assumptions that broke and the other half were resting on assumptions that did not, and a few of those matter more now than they did before.

What follows is a cleaned-up version of notes I accumulated over the past year. Gemini 4 helped with the editing.

What we actually know

The cost of producing plausible code has collapsed and it is not going back. Almost every claim beyond that is either unproven or wrong.

  • That AI tooling has made engineering orgs dramatically faster: unproven.
  • That code review, documentation, and onboarding are obsolete: wrong.
  • That you can run the same roadmap with half the people: a bet, not a fact.

If you rebuild your management practices on the narrow claim, you will be right. If you rebuild them on the broad claims you are gambling with other people's careers and calling it a conclusion.

Focus on auditing assumptions

Every management practice rests on a certain assumption. Velocity tracking rests on output being a usable proxy for effort. Six month onboarding rests on syntax being slow to learn. Consensus driven architecture rests on change being expensive. Headcount planning rests on output scaling with people, and so on.

The question for each practice is not how old it is but rather what the practice actually rests on.

If a practice rests on the cost of writing code, put it under review because that cost moved. If it rests on how humans coordinate, build trust, allocate attention, or verify correctness, then nothing about it changed, no matter how dated the ritual feels.

This sounds obvious but I think many are sorting by feel: whatever seems modern stays, whatever seems old goes. That produces teams that abandoned useful friction and kept useless process, because the age of a practice and the validity of a practice are unrelated variables.

The evidence is smaller than the noise

Be suspicious of anyone, including your own team, who reports large speedups and only that. The gains I'm familiar with show up clearly in greenfield work, boilerplate, and unfamiliar territory. They fade or invert in deep work on systems the engineer already understands. I'm very much looking forward to data and studies done after the Q4 2025, where a new breed of models were launched that completely eclipsed the capabilities of the ones older reports and research were based on.

However, the gap between felt speed and measured speed is itself a management problem. If your engineers feel faster and ship the same amount with more defects, you will staff wrong, plan wrong, and set expectations with the business that you cannot meet. The first job in an AI adopting org is instrumentation being honest enough to tell you whether you have accelerated at all.

Weak proxies for a cheap thing

Velocity, pull request counts, and tickets closed were always imperfect. They survived because the thing they approximated ie the effort of writing code was genuinely scarce, so the noise stayed within tolerable bounds.

Now the proxied thing is cheap. That does not leave the metrics merely imperfect but actually actively misleading, because the cheapest way to raise them is to generate volume, and volume is the one thing your organization no longer lacks.

AI-specific metrics solve the wrong problem. I think acceptance rates and prompt counts are the same mistake in a new form. The durable move is older and harder: measure outcomes for the business and the health of the system, and treat code volume as a cost to be justified rather than output to be praised. Good engineers said this before LLMs. It was true then. It is enforceable now in a way it was not, because nobody can argue that writing more code was the hard part.

"Right" still takes time (for now)

The rule that good work takes time splits cleanly in two.

Plumbing time collapsed. Scaffolding a service, generating tests, translating between frameworks, writing the first draft of a migration: all of this is fast now, and any timeline built on those costs deserves compression.

Correctness time splits in two

AI systems now check and correct code faster than any human reviewer, and pretending otherwise costs credibility. One one hand, mechanical verification is collapsing. Anything where correct can be expressed as a machine-checkable artifact: types, tests, contracts, lint rules, invariants, canary metrics. Agents run the test loop, read the failure, fix the diff, and run it again at a speed no reviewer matches. If your correctness lives in this layer, your checking time is genuinely falling, and it will keep falling.

But notice what makes this layer fast. It is fast because someone already wrote down what correct means, in a form a machine can evaluate. The specification did the work & the checker reads it.

Semantic verification is a different matter. Does the code implement the policy the business actually needs? Does this trade-off match your regulatory exposure? Here, correct lives in human heads and institutional history. AI checking AI has a structural problem: the checker shares training data, biases, and blind spots with the generator. Both layers fail in the same places for the same reasons. Self-review catches the typo. It does not catch the shared misunderstanding.

I believe three consequences follow, and the core of this post:

  • Unit cost falls, total workload rises. Cheap checking invites more generation, and more generation demands more checking. The verification workload grows with volume even as each individual check gets cheaper. Net calendar time is ambiguous, and the incident profile shifts: fewer dumb errors, more systemic ones, because high-volume plausible output now passes high-volume plausible review.
  • The boundary is a strategic variable. How much of your correctness is machine-checkable is not fixed. It is a function of your specifications, contracts, and invariants. Teams with strong specs get the full benefit of cheap checking. Teams with weak specs get generated code reviewed by the same machine that generated it. Investing in machine-checkable correctness is now among the highest-leverage infrastructure work an org can fund, because it sets how much of this wave you can actually use.
  • The slowest part of verification was never the checking but accountability. Someone signs & someone absorbs the consequence of being wrong: the incident review, the regulator, the customer. Sign-off time does not compress, because it is not information processing. It is risk acceptance, and legal and trust systems assign that to people.

So verification still sets throughput. What moved is the location of the constraint: from checking speed to specification quality, and to the willingness of a specific human to own the result.

The junior pipeline is an unsolved problem

Nobody knows how to train engineers for this environment.

The judgment you want in a senior engineer was historically built by doing the work that AI now absorbs: fixing small bugs, writing boilerplate, getting stuck and then unstuck: these were not just tasks but actually the practice that produced judgment. If the machine takes the practice, the pipeline that produces seniors breaks, and it breaks on a delay, so you will not notice for three to five years.

There are plausible responses. Structured review of generated code, deliberate unassisted exercises, rotations through testing and verification work, earlier exposure to real systems under close senior oversight. I am running versions of some of these. I cannot tell you they work, because the outcome variable is the quality of a senior engineer half a decade from now.

What I can tell you is that anyone who claims to have solved this, whether vendor, essayist, or conference speaker, is selling something. Treat the pipeline as an open problem you personally own. It has the longest delay between action and evidence, and the fewest chances to correct course.

My take on the old rules

"A director should not code." The director who dabbles, reviews pull requests to feel useful, and becomes a bottleneck is real. So is the director whose mental model of the work is five years stale, who cannot tell the difference between a team that is genuinely faster and a team that is generating confident, wrong output at volume (slop cannons). The resolution is calibration. You do not need to ship. You need enough direct contact with the tools and the output that you cannot be fooled in either direction, by the hype or by the dismissal.

"Shield the team from the business." The assumption underneath this one is that attention is finite and context switching is expensive. That assumption is intact. What changed is the cost of starving the team of context. Engineers prompting AI tools without business context just produce fluent, plausible, wrong work, at scale. The revision is not to flood everyone with everything but to stop filtering by default and start selecting deliberately: which context, to whom, at what level of detail.

"We need consensus before we commit." Consensus was always about commitment and coordination, and the cost of surviving cheap pivots. What cheap pivots change is which decisions need consensus at all. Reversible decisions, or two-way doors, should be made by the smallest group possible, quickly, because a wrong reversible call is now cheap to undo. Irreversible decisions still deserve the slow process. The actual skill is classification, and most organizations misclassify constantly, treating reversible technical choices as permanent and permanent organizational choices as casual.

"We need more headcount." The unit economics of output changed, so every request deserves a harder question than it got three years ago: what part of this work is judgment, and what part is production we keep hiring humans to do? But do not overcorrect. Adding people to a late project still makes it later. Coordination cost, onboarding drag, and communication overhead did not change with the price of syntax. Scrutinize headcount because output per person moved, not because people stopped being the expensive part.

Why the tropes persist

Three years in, here is what I believe about persistence. Practices survive for reasons, and the reasons are always mixed: some obsolete, some still valid, some political. When you hear an old rule repeated, you are usually hearing a person defend the valid part with the wrong argument or defend the obsolete part with the argument that used to work.

Treating persistence as stupidity is the failure mode of every management fashion, and the AI fashion is not exempt. The leaders who will look worst in five years are not the cautious ones but the ones who replaced thinking with a new set of slogans, even accurate sounding slogans, and ran their orgs on claims that were still unmeasured.

The job is sorting

The temptation, when a technology this large arrives, is to pick a posture: burn the old playbook or defend it. Both postures are laziness. The playbook was never a single object. It was a hundred pages, some about the cost of typing and some about the nature of people, bound together so tightly that we forgot they were separable.

Do not let anyone, including a confident essay, including this one, convince you those were ever the same page.

Will the machines do the sorting

I was told recently that AIs will soon do the management too, including the sorting. I thought about it over the weekend and I believe it is partly right.

Management has an information-routing function: aggregating status, tracking progress, translating updates into dashboards, forecasting schedules, collating performance data. A large share of what a management layer does daily is moving information between formats and people. LLMs are excellent at this, and the value of this is going to zero. If your management layer earns its keep by summarizing Jira, then yeah, that's over.

Then there is the judgment function: hiring, firing, promotion, deciding which rule applies in this situation with these people, owning a bad call. This has the same structure as verification. Someone checks the output against reality, and someone absorbs the consequence.

We're back to the generation argument mentionned above, but applied to management work: management output becomes abundant, therefore cheap. But the thesis of everything above is that when generation is abundant, verification is the constraint. Machine-generated management still needs a human to verify it against the org's actual behavior and to sign the result. So this is perhaps not the end of the manager but rather the manager's demotion to editor and owner. It is the exact same shift the individual contributor is going through.

There is one more problem with delegating the sorting. Sorting requires a model of how your org actually behaves: trust relationships, hallway knowledge, the consequences of past decisions. Almost none of this is written down. The written record of an org is a small, polished fraction of the org, and a model sorts on the record. Worse, what the model encodes from its training is the industry's average judgment. An LLM will sort your playbook roughly the way the median org would. If your strategy is to be the median org, that is fine. Differentiation lives exactly in the decisions you refuse to delegate.

Here is my honest concession, the sorting as an intellectual exercise is automatable. I used AI to pressure-test parts of this essay, and its first-pass audit was decent. What is not automatable is the political and moral work.

Where this goes: spans of control widen, layers compress, the information-routing tier of management is genuinely at risk, and titles will persist longer than functions. The management work that survives is the work that cannot be written down, cannot be averaged, and cannot be signed by anyone else.

What survives

The residual of engineering work is specification and ownership. The residual of management work is judgment and ownership. Same shape, two levels.

At every level of the org, the work that survives is the work someone has to sign.

Let's push the extrapolation to its limit to really drive it home. Imagine an org where agents write the code, run the checks, route the status, schedule the work, and draft the plans. Humans set direction, define what correct means, and sign. Everything between the signature and the shipped result is machinery. Now run the timeline backwards: imagine this org came first, and someone proposed the one you actually run. We will hire hundreds of expensive people to produce text by hand, at typing speed. We will arrange them in layers, where the job of each layer is to summarize the layer below for the layer above. We will synchronize their calendars in rooms so they can tell each other what already happened. We will measure their worth by how much they emit. Nobody would fund this proposal. It is slow, it loses information at every handoff, and it spends the scarcest resource in the building on work the machinery already does.

The org you run was never designed but it rather accumulated. Every role, ritual, and layer exists because something used to be expensive: typing, routing, checking, remembering. The prices moved. The org chart did not. In the agentic limit, the chart stops recording who produces and starts recording who signs. Headcount stops measuring capacity and starts measuring how much accountability you can afford. The orgs that get there will look small, quiet, and mostly empty: a short list of names attached to a long list of decisions, and nothing else left to manage.

sentences.en: If you rebuild your management practices on the narrow claim, you will be right.

sentences.en: If you rebuild them on the broad claims you are gambling with other people's careers and calling it a conclusion.
sentences.zh: 如果你根据宽泛的主张重建它们，那么你就是在拿别人的职业生涯赌博，并称之为结论。

blocks.html_en: Focus on auditing assumptions

sentences.en: Focus on auditing assumptions
sentences.zh: 关注审计假设

blocks.html_en: Every management practice rests on a certain assumption. Velocity tracking rests on output being a usable proxy for effort. Six month onboarding rests on syntax being slow to learn. Consensus driven architecture rests on change being expensive. Headcount planning rests on output scaling with people, and so on.

sentences.en: Every management practice rests on a certain assumption.
sentences.zh: 每个管理实践都基于一定的假设。

sentences.en: Velocity tracking rests on output being a usable proxy for effort.
sentences.zh: 速度跟踪依赖于输出作为工作量的可用代理。

sentences.en: Six month onboarding rests on syntax being slow to learn.
sentences.zh: 六个月的入职时间取决于语法学习速度缓慢。

sentences.en: Consensus driven architecture rests on change being expensive.
sentences.zh: 共识驱动的架构依赖于昂贵的变更。

sentences.en: Headcount planning rests on output scaling with people, and so on.
sentences.zh: 员工人数规划取决于人员的产出规模等。

blocks.html_en: The question for each practice is not how old it is but rather what the practice actually rests on.

sentences.en: The question for each practice is not how old it is but rather what the practice actually rests on.
sentences.zh: 每个实践的问题不在于其历史有多久，而在于该实践实际上基于什么。

blocks.html_en: If a practice rests on the cost of writing code, put it under review because that cost moved. If it rests on how humans coordinate, build trust, allocate attention, or verify correctness, then nothing about it changed, no matter how dated the ritual feels.

sentences.en: If a practice rests on the cost of writing code, put it under review because that cost moved.
sentences.zh: 如果某项实践依赖于编写代码的成本，请对其进行审查，因为该成本已转移。

sentences.en: If it rests on how humans coordinate, build trust, allocate attention, or verify correctness, then nothing about it changed, no matter how dated the ritual feels.
sentences.zh: 如果它取决于人类如何协调、建立信任、分配注意力或验证正确性，那么无论仪式感觉多么过时，它都不会改变。

blocks.html_en: This sounds obvious but I think many are sorting by feel: whatever seems modern stays, whatever seems old goes. That produces teams that abandoned useful friction and kept useless process, because the age of a practice and the validity of a practice are unrelated variables.

sentences.en: This sounds obvious but I think many are sorting by feel: whatever seems modern stays, whatever seems old goes.

sentences.en: That produces teams that abandoned useful friction and kept useless process, because the age of a practice and the validity of a practice are unrelated variables.
sentences.zh: 这就产生了放弃有用摩擦并保留无用流程的团队，因为实践的年龄和实践的有效性是不相关的变量。

blocks.html_en: The evidence is smaller than the noise

sentences.en: The evidence is smaller than the noise
sentences.zh: 证据比噪音小

The gains I'm familiar with show up clearly in greenfield work, boilerplate, and unfamiliar territory. They fade or invert in deep work on systems the engineer already understands. I'm very much looking forward to data and studies done after the Q4 2025, where a new breed of models were launched that completely eclipsed the capabilities of the ones older reports and research were based on.

sentences.en: Be suspicious of anyone, including your own team, who reports large speedups and only that.

sentences.en: The gains I'm familiar with show up clearly in greenfield work, boilerplate, and unfamiliar territory.

The first job in an AI adopting org is instrumentation being honest enough to tell you whether you have accelerated at all.

sentences.en: However, the gap between felt speed and measured speed is itself a management problem.

sentences.en: If your engineers feel faster and ship the same amount with more defects, you will staff wrong, plan wrong, and set expectations with the business that you cannot meet.
sentences.zh: 如果您的工程师感觉速度更快，但交付相同数量的产品却有更多缺陷，那么您就会用错人员，制定错误的计划，并对业务设定无法满足的期望。

sentences.en: The first job in an AI adopting org is instrumentation being honest enough to tell you whether you have accelerated at all.
sentences.zh: 在采用人工智能的组织中，第一项工作是仪器足够诚实地告诉你是否已经加速了。

blocks.html_en: Weak proxies for a cheap thing

sentences.en: Weak proxies for a cheap thing
sentences.zh: 便宜的东西的弱代理

blocks.html_en: Velocity, pull request counts, and tickets closed were always imperfect. They survived because the thing they approximated ie the effort of writing code was genuinely scarce, so the noise stayed within tolerable bounds.

sentences.en: Velocity, pull request counts, and tickets closed were always imperfect.
sentences.zh: 速度、拉取请求计数和关闭的票证总是不完美的。

sentences.en: They survived because the thing they approximated ie the effort of writing code was genuinely scarce, so the noise stayed within tolerable bounds.
sentences.zh: 他们幸存下来是因为他们所近似的东西，即编写代码的努力确实很少，因此噪音保持在可容忍的范围内。

blocks.html_en: Now the proxied thing is cheap. That does not leave the metrics merely imperfect but actually actively misleading, because the cheapest way to raise them is to generate volume, and volume is the one thing your organization no longer lacks.

sentences.en: Now the proxied thing is cheap.
sentences.zh: 现在代理的东西很便宜。

blocks.html_en: AI-specific metrics solve the wrong problem. I think acceptance rates and prompt counts are the same mistake in a new form. Good engineers said this before LLMs. It was true then. It is enforceable now in a way it was not, because nobody can argue that writing more code was the hard part.

sentences.en: AI-specific metrics solve the wrong problem.
sentences.zh: 人工智能特定的指标解决了错误的问题。

sentences.en: I think acceptance rates and prompt counts are the same mistake in a new form.
sentences.zh: 我认为接受率和提示计数在新形式中是同一个错误。

sentences.en: The durable move is older and harder: measure outcomes for the business and the health of the system, and treat code volume as a cost to be justified rather than output to be praised.
sentences.zh: 持久的举措更古老、更困难：衡量业务结果和系统的健康状况，并将代码量视为合理的成本，而不是值得赞扬的产出。

sentences.en: Good engineers said this before LLMs.
sentences.zh: 优秀的工程师在法学硕士之前说过这句话。

sentences.en: It was true then.
sentences.zh: 那时确实如此。

sentences.en: It is enforceable now in a way it was not, because nobody can argue that writing more code was the hard part.
sentences.zh: 它现在以一种以前不可以的方式强制执行，因为没有人会说编写更多代码是困难的部分。

blocks.html_en: "Right" still takes time (for now)

sentences.en: "Right" still takes time (for now)
sentences.zh: “正确”还需要时间（目前）

blocks.html_en: The rule that good work takes time splits cleanly in two.

sentences.en: The rule that good work takes time splits cleanly in two.
sentences.zh: 好的工作需要时间这一规则被一分为二。

blocks.html_en: Plumbing time collapsed. Scaffolding a service, generating tests, translating between frameworks, writing the first draft of a migration: all of this is fast now, and any timeline built on those costs deserves compression.

sentences.en: Plumbing time collapsed.
sentences.zh: 水管时间崩溃了。

sentences.en: Scaffolding a service, generating tests, translating between frameworks, writing the first draft of a migration: all of this is fast now, and any timeline built on those costs deserves compression.
sentences.zh: 搭建服务、生成测试、在框架之间进行转换、编写迁移的初稿：所有这些现在都很快，并且基于这些成本构建的任何时间表都值得压缩。

blocks.html_en: Correctness time splits in two

sentences.en: Correctness time splits in two
sentences.zh: 正确性时间一分为二

blocks.html_en: AI systems now check and correct code faster than any human reviewer, and pretending otherwise costs credibility. One one hand, mechanical verification is collapsing. Anything where correct can be expressed as a machine-checkable artifact: types, tests, contracts, lint rules, invariants, canary metrics. Agents run the test loop, read the failure, fix the diff, and run it again at a speed no reviewer matches. If your correctness lives in this layer, your checking time is genuinely falling, and it will keep falling.

sentences.en: AI systems now check and correct code faster than any human reviewer, and pretending otherwise costs credibility.
sentences.zh: 人工智能系统现在检查和更正代码的速度比任何人类审阅者都快，否则假装会降低可信度。

sentences.en: One one hand, mechanical verification is collapsing.
sentences.zh: 一方面，机械验证正在崩溃。

sentences.en: Anything where correct can be expressed as a machine-checkable artifact: types, tests, contracts, lint rules, invariants, canary metrics.
sentences.zh: 任何正确的东西都可以表示为机器可检查的工件：类型、测试、契约、lint 规则、不变量、金丝雀指标。

sentences.en: Agents run the test loop, read the failure, fix the diff, and run it again at a speed no reviewer matches.
sentences.zh: 代理运行测试循环，读取故障，修复差异，然后以审阅者无法匹敌的速度再次运行。

sentences.en: If your correctness lives in this layer, your checking time is genuinely falling, and it will keep falling.
sentences.zh: 如果你的正确性存在于这一层，那么你的检查时间确实会下降，而且会继续下降。

blocks.html_en: But notice what makes this layer fast. It is fast because someone already wrote down what correct means, in a form a machine can evaluate. The specification did the work & the checker reads it.

sentences.en: But notice what makes this layer fast.
sentences.zh: 但请注意是什么让这一层变得更快。

sentences.en: It is fast because someone already wrote down what correct means, in a form a machine can evaluate.
sentences.zh: 它很快，因为有人已经以机器可以评估的形式写下了正确的含义。

sentences.en: The specification did the work & the checker reads it.
sentences.zh: 规范完成了工作，检查员读取了它。

blocks.html_en: Semantic verification is a different matter. Does the code implement the policy the business actually needs? Does this trade-off match your regulatory exposure? Both layers fail in the same places for the same reasons. Self-review catches the typo. It does not catch the shared misunderstanding.

sentences.en: Semantic verification is a different matter.
sentences.zh: 语义验证是另一回事。

sentences.en: Does the code implement the policy the business actually needs?
sentences.zh: 代码是否实现了业务实际需要的策略？

sentences.en: Does this trade-off match your regulatory exposure?
sentences.zh: 这种权衡是否符合您的监管要求？

sentences.en: Here, correct lives in human heads and institutional history.
sentences.zh: 在这里，正确的生活存在于人类头脑和制度历史中。

sentences.en: AI checking AI has a structural problem: the checker shares training data, biases, and blind spots with the generator.
sentences.zh: 人工智能检查人工智能有一个结构性问题：检查器与生成器共享训练数据、偏差和盲点。

sentences.en: Both layers fail in the same places for the same reasons.
sentences.zh: 由于相同的原因，这两层都在相同的位置失败。

sentences.en: Self-review catches the typo.
sentences.zh: 自我审查发现了拼写错误。

sentences.en: It does not catch the shared misunderstanding.
sentences.zh: 它没有抓住共同的误解。

blocks.html_en: I believe three consequences follow, and the core of this post:

sentences.en: I believe three consequences follow, and the core of this post:
sentences.zh: 我相信会产生三个后果，也是这篇文章的核心：

blocks.html_en: • Unit cost falls, total workload rises. Cheap checking invites more generation, and more generation demands more checking. The verification workload grows with volume even as each individual check gets cheaper. Net calendar time is ambiguous, and the incident profile shifts: fewer dumb errors, more systemic ones, because high-volume plausible output now passes high-volume plausible review.

sentences.en: Unit cost falls, total workload rises.
sentences.zh: 单位成本下降，总工作量增加。

sentences.en: Cheap checking invites more generation, and more generation demands more checking.
sentences.zh: 廉价的检查会吸引更多的一代，而更多的一代又需要更多的检查。

sentences.en: The verification workload grows with volume even as each individual check gets cheaper.
sentences.zh: 即使每项单独的检查变得更便宜，验证工作量也会随着数量的增加而增加。

sentences.en: Net calendar time is ambiguous, and the incident profile shifts: fewer dumb errors, more systemic ones, because high-volume plausible output now passes high-volume plausible review.
sentences.zh: 净日历时间不明确，事件概况发生变化：愚蠢的错误更少，系统性错误更多，因为大量合理的输出现在通过了大量合理的审查。

blocks.html_en: • The boundary is a strategic variable. How much of your correctness is machine-checkable is not fixed. It is a function of your specifications, contracts, and invariants. Teams with strong specs get the full benefit of cheap checking. Teams with weak specs get generated code reviewed by the same machine that generated it. Investing in machine-checkable correctness is now among the highest-leverage infrastructure work an org can fund, because it sets how much of this wave you can actually use.

sentences.en: The boundary is a strategic variable.
sentences.zh: 边界是一个战略变量。

sentences.en: How much of your correctness is machine-checkable is not fixed.
sentences.zh: 机器可检查的正确性有多少是不确定的。

sentences.en: It is a function of your specifications, contracts, and invariants.
sentences.zh: 它是您的规范、契约和不变量的函数。

sentences.en: Teams with strong specs get the full benefit of cheap checking.
sentences.zh: 具有强大规格的团队可以充分享受廉价检查的好处。

sentences.en: Teams with weak specs get generated code reviewed by the same machine that generated it.
sentences.zh: 规格较弱的团队可以通过生成代码的同一台机器来审查生成的代码。

sentences.en: Investing in machine-checkable correctness is now among the highest-leverage infrastructure work an org can fund, because it sets how much of this wave you can actually use.
sentences.zh: 投资机器可检查的正确性现在是组织可以资助的最高杠杆基础设施工作之一，因为它决定了您可以实际使用的浪潮的数量。

blocks.html_en: • The slowest part of verification was never the checking but accountability. Someone signs & someone absorbs the consequence of being wrong: the incident review, the regulator, the customer. Sign-off time does not compress, because it is not information processing. It is risk acceptance, and legal and trust systems assign that to people.

sentences.en: The slowest part of verification was never the checking but accountability.
sentences.zh: 验证过程中最慢的部分从来不是检查，而是问责。

sentences.en: Someone signs & someone absorbs the consequence of being wrong: the incident review, the regulator, the customer.
sentences.zh: 有人签字并承担错误的后果：事件审查、监管机构、客户。

sentences.en: Sign-off time does not compress, because it is not information processing.

sentences.en: It is risk acceptance, and legal and trust systems assign that to people.
sentences.zh: 这是风险接受，法律和信任系统将其分配给人们。

blocks.html_en: So verification still sets throughput. What moved is the location of the constraint: from checking speed to specification quality, and to the willingness of a specific human to own the result.

sentences.en: So verification still sets throughput.
sentences.zh: 所以验证仍然决定吞吐量。

sentences.en: What moved is the location of the constraint: from checking speed to specification quality, and to the willingness of a specific human to own the result.
sentences.zh: 改变的是约束的位置：从检查速度到规格质量，再到特定人员拥有结果的意愿。

blocks.html_en: The junior pipeline is an unsolved problem

sentences.en: The junior pipeline is an unsolved problem
sentences.zh: 初级管道是一个未解决的问题

blocks.html_en: Nobody knows how to train engineers for this environment.

sentences.en: Nobody knows how to train engineers for this environment.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道如何针对这种环境培训工程师。

blocks.html_en: The judgment you want in a senior engineer was historically built by doing the work that AI now absorbs: fixing small bugs, writing boilerplate, getting stuck and then unstuck: these were not just tasks but actually the practice that produced judgment. If the machine takes the practice, the pipeline that produces seniors breaks, and it breaks on a delay, so you will not notice for three to five years.

sentences.en: If the machine takes the practice, the pipeline that produces seniors breaks, and it breaks on a delay, so you will not notice for three to five years.
sentences.zh: 如果机器练习的话，生产高级的管道坏了，而且是延迟坏的，所以三五年你都不会注意到。

blocks.html_en: "A director should not code." The director who dabbles, reviews pull requests to feel useful, and becomes a bottleneck is real. So is the director whose mental model of the work is five years stale, who cannot tell the difference between a team that is genuinely faster and a team that is generating confident, wrong output at volume (slop cannons). The resolution is calibration. You do not need to ship. You need enough direct contact with the tools and the output that you cannot be fooled in either direction, by the hype or by the dismissal.

blocks.html_en: "Shield the team from the business." The assumption underneath this one is that attention is finite and context switching is expensive. That assumption is intact. What changed is the cost of starving the team of context. Engineers prompting AI tools without business context just produce fluent, plausible, wrong work, at scale. The revision is not to flood everyone with everything but to stop filtering by default and start selecting deliberately: which context, to whom, at what level of detail.

content_html_zh:
我担任工程总监已有三年多了，我仍然听到并读到一遍又一遍重复的我所说的“旧规则”：总监不应该花时间编码，好的工作需要时间，保护团队免受业务影响，在承诺之前达成共识等等。

有一段时间我认为那些重复这些台词的人已经落后了。 然后我们在我的组织中引入了法学硕士，生成代码的成本下降了，我开始根据其背后的假设检查每条规则。 令人惊讶的认识是，大约一半的旧规则建立在已被打破的假设之上，另一半则建立在没有被打破的假设之上，其中一些规则现在比以前更重要。

以下是我过去一年积累的笔记的清理版本。 Gemini 4 帮助进行了编辑。

我们实际上知道什么

生成合理代码的成本已经大幅下降，而且不会再下降。 除此之外，几乎所有的说法要么未经证实，要么是错误的。

  • 人工智能工具使工程组织的速度大大加快：未经证实。
  • 代码审查、文档和入门已经过时：错误的。
  • 你可以与一半的人运行相同的路线图：这是一个赌注，而不是事实。

如果你根据狭隘的主张重建你的管理实践，你就是对的。 如果你根据宽泛的主张重建它们，那么你就是在拿别人的职业生涯赌博，并称之为结论。

关注审计假设

每个管理实践都基于一定的假设。 速度跟踪依赖于输出作为工作量的可用代理。 六个月的入职时间取决于语法学习速度缓慢。 共识驱动的架构依赖于昂贵的变更。 员工人数规划取决于人员的产出规模等。

每个实践的问题不在于其历史有多久，而在于该实践实际上基于什么。

如果某项实践依赖于编写代码的成本，请对其进行审查，因为该成本已转移。 如果它取决于人类如何协调、建立信任、分配注意力或验证正确性，那么无论仪式感觉多么过时，它都不会改变。

这听起来很明显，但我认为很多人都是根据感觉来排序的：任何看起来现代的东西都会留下，任何看起来旧的东西都会消失。 这就产生了放弃有用摩擦并保留无用流程的团队，因为实践的年龄和实践的有效性是不相关的变量。

证据比噪音小

对报告大幅加速的任何人（包括您自己的团队）保持怀疑。 我所熟悉的收获在新手工作、样板文件和不熟悉的领域中清晰地体现出来。 它们在工程师已经了解的系统的深入工作中逐渐消失或反转。 我非常期待 2025 年第四季度之后完成的数据和研究，届时推出了一种新型模型，其功能完全超越了旧报告和研究所基于的模型的能力。

然而，感觉到的速度和测量的速度之间的差距本身就是一个管理问题。 如果您的工程师感觉速度更快，但交付相同数量的产品却有更多缺陷，那么您就会用错人员，制定错误的计划，并对业务设定无法满足的期望。 在采用人工智能的组织中，第一项工作是仪器足够诚实地告诉你是否已经加速了。

便宜的东西的弱代理

速度、拉取请求计数和关闭的票证总是不完美的。 他们幸存下来是因为他们所近似的东西，即编写代码的努力确实很少，因此噪音保持在可容忍的范围内。

现在代理的东西很便宜。 这并不会让这些指标仅仅不完美，而且实际上会产生误导，因为提高这些指标的最便宜的方法是产生数量，而数量是您的组织不再缺乏的东西。

人工智能特定的指标解决了错误的问题。 我认为接受率和提示计数在新形式中是同一个错误。 持久的举措更古老、更困难：衡量业务结果和系统的健康状况，并将代码量视为合理的成本，而不是值得赞扬的产出。 优秀的工程师在法学硕士之前说过这句话。 那时确实如此。 它现在以一种以前不可以的方式强制执行，因为没有人会说编写更多代码是困难的部分。

“正确”还需要时间（目前）

好的工作需要时间这一规则被一分为二。

水管时间崩溃了。 搭建服务、生成测试、在框架之间进行转换、编写迁移的初稿：所有这些现在都很快，并且基于这些成本构建的任何时间表都值得压缩。

正确性时间一分为二

人工智能系统现在检查和更正代码的速度比任何人类审阅者都快，否则假装会降低可信度。 一方面，机械验证正在崩溃。 任何正确的东西都可以表示为机器可检查的工件：类型、测试、契约、lint 规则、不变量、金丝雀指标。 代理运行测试循环，读取故障，修复差异，然后以审阅者无法匹敌的速度再次运行。 如果你的正确性存在于这一层，那么你的检查时间确实会下降，而且会继续下降。

但请注意是什么让这一层变得更快。 它很快，因为有人已经以机器可以评估的形式写下了正确的含义。 规范完成了工作，检查员读取了它。

语义验证是另一回事。 代码是否实现了业务实际需要的策略？ 这种权衡是否符合您的监管要求？ 在这里，正确的生活存在于人类头脑和制度历史中。 人工智能检查人工智能有一个结构性问题：检查器与生成器共享训练数据、偏差和盲点。 由于相同的原因，这两层都在相同的位置失败。 自我审查发现了拼写错误。 它没有抓住共同的误解。

我相信会产生三个后果，也是这篇文章的核心：

  • 单位成本下降，总工作量增加。 廉价的检查会吸引更多的一代，而更多的一代又需要更多的检查。 即使每项单独的检查变得更便宜，验证工作量也会随着数量的增加而增加。 净日历时间不明确，事件概况发生变化：愚蠢的错误更少，系统性错误更多，因为大量合理的输出现在通过了大量合理的审查。
  • 边界是一个战略变量。 机器可检查的正确性有多少是不确定的。 它是您的规范、契约和不变量的函数。 具有强大规格的团队可以充分享受廉价检查的好处。 规格较弱的团队可以通过生成代码的同一台机器来审查生成的代码。 投资机器可检查的正确性现在是组织可以资助的最高杠杆基础设施工作之一，因为它决定了您可以实际使用的浪潮的数量。
  • 验证过程中最慢的部分从来不是检查，而是问责。 有人签字并承担错误的后果：事件审查、监管机构、客户。 签核时间不会压缩，因为它不是信息处理。 这是风险接受，法律和信任系统将其分配给人们。

所以验证仍然决定吞吐量。 改变的是约束的位置：从检查速度到规格质量，再到特定人员拥有结果的意愿。

初级管道是一个未解决的问题

没有人知道如何针对这种环境培训工程师。

历史上，你想要的高级工程师的判断力是通过人工智能现在吸收的工作来建立的：修复小错误，编写样板文件，陷入困境然后摆脱困境：这些不仅仅是任务，而且实际上是产生判断力的实践。 如果机器练习的话，生产高级的管道坏了，而且是延迟坏的，所以三五年你都不会注意到。

有一些看似合理的回应。 对生成的代码进行结构化审查，深思熟虑的独立练习，通过测试和验证工作进行轮换，在高层的密切监督下尽早接触真实系统。 我正在运行其中一些版本。 我不能告诉你它们有效，因为结果变量是五年后高级工程师的质量。

我可以告诉你的是，任何声称已经解决了这个问题的人，无论是供应商、散文家还是会议发言人，都在推销一些东西。 将管道视为您个人拥有的开放问题。 它在行动和证据之间的延迟最长，并且纠正方向的机会最少。

我对旧规则的看法

“导演不应该编码。” 主管涉猎、审查拉取请求以感觉有用，并成为瓶颈，这是真实的。 导演的工作心智模型已经过时了五年，他无法区分真正更快的团队和自信地产生错误产量的团队（垃圾炮）之间的区别。 分辨率是校准。 您不需要运送。 您需要与工具和输出有足够的直接接触，这样您就不会被任何一个方向所欺骗，无论是炒作还是解雇。

“保护团队免受业务影响。” 这一假设背后的假设是注意力是有限的并且上下文切换是昂贵的。 这个假设是完整的。 改变的是团队缺乏背景的成本。 工程师在没有业务背景的情况下使用人工智能工具只会大规模地产生流畅、合理、错误的工作。 此次修订并不是让每个人都充斥着一切，而是停止默认过滤并开始刻意选择：哪个上下文、针对谁、以何种详细程度进行选择。

“在我们做出承诺之前，我们需要达成共识。” 共识始终涉及承诺和协调，以及廉价转型的生存成本。 廉价的枢纽改变的是哪些决策需要达成共识。 可逆决策或双向门应由尽可能小的小组快速做出，因为现在撤消错误的可逆调用的成本很低。 不可逆转的决定仍然需要缓慢的过程。 实际的技能是分类，大多数组织不断地错误分类，将可逆的技术选择视为永久性的，而将永久性的组织选择视为随意的。

“我们需要更多的人手。” 产出的单位经济学发生了变化，因此每一个请求都需要一个比三年前更难的问题：这项工作的哪一部分是判断，哪一部分是我们一直雇用人类来做的生产？ 但不要矫枉过正。 将人员添加到较晚的项目中仍然会让项目变得更晚。 协调成本、入门阻力和沟通开销并没有随着语法的价格而改变。 审查员工人数是因为人均产出发生了变化，而不是因为人不再是昂贵的部分。

为什么这些比喻持续存在

三年过去了，这就是我对坚持的信念。 实践之所以能够存在，是有原因的，而原因总是混杂的：有些已经过时，有些仍然有效，有些是政治性的。 当你听到重复一条旧规则时，你通常会听到有人用错误的论据来捍卫有效的部分，或者用曾经有效的论据来捍卫过时的部分。

将坚持视为愚蠢是每一种管理时尚的失败模式，人工智能时尚也不例外。 五年后看起来最糟糕的领导者不是那些谨慎的领导者，而是那些用一套新的口号甚至听起来准确的口号取代思维的人，并根据仍然无法衡量的主张来管理他们的组织。

工作正在整理

当如此大规模的技术到来时，人们往往会选择一种态度：烧掉旧的剧本或捍卫它。 这两种姿势都是懒惰的。 剧本从来就不是一个单一的对象。 它有一百页，有些是关于打字的成本，有些是关于人的本性，紧紧地结合在一起，以至于我们忘记了它们是可以分开的。

不要让任何人，包括一篇自信的文章，包括这篇文章，让你相信这些文章是同一页的。

机器会进行分类吗

最近有人告诉我，人工智能很快也会进行管理，包括分类。 我周末思考了一下，我相信它是部分正确的。

管理层具有信息路由功能：汇总状态、跟踪进度、将更新转换为仪表板、预测时间表、整理绩效数据。 管理层日常工作的很大一部分是在格式和人员之间移动信息。 法学硕士在这方面非常出色，但其价值将为零。 如果您的管理层通过总结 Jira 来维持生计，那么是的，一切都结束了。

然后是判断功能：雇用、解雇、晋升，决定在这些人的这种情况下适用哪种规则，拥有一个糟糕的决定。 这与验证具有相同的结构。 有人根据现实检查输出，有人吸收结果。

我们回到上面提到的世代论点，但应用于管理工作：管理产出变得丰富，因此便宜。 但以上所有内容的论点是，当生成丰富时，验证就是约束。 机器生成的管理仍然需要人工根据组织的实际行为进行验证并签署结果。 所以这也许不是经理的终结，而是经理被降级为编辑和所有者。 这与个人贡献者正在经历的转变完全相同。

委托排序还有一个问题。 排序需要一个关于您的组织实际行为方式的模型：信任关系、走廊知识、过去决策的后果。 这些几乎都没有被记录下来。 组织的书面记录是组织的一小部分，经过精心打磨，模型对记录进行排序。 更糟糕的是，模型从训练中编码的是行业的平均判断。 法学硕士将大致按照中位数组织的方式对您的剧本进行排序。 如果您的策略是成为中等组织，那就没问题。 差异化恰恰存在于你拒绝授权的决策中。

这是我诚实的让步，排序作为一项智力练习是可以自动化的。 我使用人工智能对这篇文章的部分内容进行了压力测试，其首次通过审核还不错。 政治和道德工作是不可自动化的。

未来的发展方向是：控制范围扩大，层级压缩，信息路由管理层真正面临风险，头衔将比职能持续更长时间。 幸存下来的管理工作是不能被写下来、不能被平均、不能被其他人签字的工作。

什么幸存下来

工程工作的剩余部分是规范和所有权。 管理工作剩下的就是判断力和所有权。 形状相同，两层。

在组织的每个级别，幸存的工作都是必须有人签名的工作。

让我们将外推推至极限，以真正理解它。 想象一个组织，其中代理编写代码、运行检查、路由状态、安排工作并起草计划。 人类设定方向、定义正确的含义并签署。 签名和交付结果之间的一切都是机械的。 现在向后运行时间线：想象一下这个组织是第一个出现的，有人提出了您实际运行的组织。 我们将雇用数百名昂贵的人员以打字速度手工生成文本。 我们将它们分层排列，每一层的工作就是为上面的层总结下面的层。 我们将在房间里同步他们的日历，以便他们可以互相告诉对方已经发生了什么。 我们将通过它们的排放量来衡量它们的价值。 没有人愿意资助这个提案。 它速度很慢，每次切换都会丢失信息，并且将建筑物中最稀缺的资源花费在机器已经完成的工作上。

你运营的组织从来都不是设计出来的，而是积累出来的。 每个角色、仪式和层级的存在都是因为过去有些东西很昂贵：打字、路由、检查、记忆。 价格发生了变化。 组织结构图没有。 在代理限制下，图表停止记录谁制作并开始记录谁签名。 员工人数不再衡量能力，而是开始衡量你能承担多少责任。 到达那里的组织将看起来小、安静，而且大多是空的：一个简短的名字列表附加在一长串的决策上，没有其他需要管理的了。
